newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher on Friday, buoyed by gains in other debt markets after U.S. Q4 GDP data revealed a better-than-expected price deflator, dealers said.
The 10-year cash spread over Bunds also recovered ending at around 92 basis points after touching 97 bps earlier.
But dealers said recent volatility and a weaker peseta were shedding a different light on Spain's market.
"In the short run sentiment is different. In recent days people are not as positive that Spain will be in EMU from the start as before" said Valentin Fernandez at Credit Lyonnais.
The peseta stood at 84.63/68 per mark in late trade, from 84.55/60 late on Thursday. Earlier, the Bank of Spain was seen selling marks for pesetas when the Spanish currency hit a low around 84.71.

In the coming week, the main focus should remain with the U.S. Federal Open Market Commitee, which will meet on February 4 and 5. Domestically, dealers expect pressure at the longer end as a result of the forthcoming auctions next week.
